findings: Non-blocking (latent, dead code): getEksClientForTokenGeneration(CloudAccount) now caches on a region-only key 'HOST_TOKEN:EksClient:<region>' but the cached client bakes in that first account's getCredentialsProvider(account) (role ARN + external ID) and getClientOverrideConfig(account,...) (per-account permission interceptor stamp). If this method ever gets a caller that passes more than one CloudAccount, every call after the first returns a client authenticated as the FIRST account — a cross-account correctness bug. It is currently unreachable (zero callers in the repo), so it is not an active regression, and it matches the approved FEAT-001 plan. Recommend keying per account (e.g. account.getAwsAccountId()+':EksClient:'+region) before wiring up any caller.

Informational (not a regression): In AzurePerformanceService.fetchFromAdvisor and AzureAlertsService.fetchFromMonitor, a non-200/non-403 failure on a LATER pagination page is now swallowed by armClient.list (which uses getQuietly after page 1) and returns the partial results as OK, whereas the old hand-rolled loop returned API_ERROR on any page's non-200. First-page failures are still mapped to PERMISSION_ERROR/API_ERROR exactly as before. This is an acceptable, arguably-better behavior consistent with the shared-client contract.

Scope note (not part of the thread-leak fix): the branch also carries three unrelated commits (security findings snapshot persist, XamSecure posture dedupe, Security Center group read-from-live) that touch SecurityController.java and SecurityAggregationService.java. These were not in the thread-leak review scope; they compile and their tests (SecurityControllerSnapshotPersistTest, AzureSecurityAggregationServiceTest) pass, but they should be reviewed on their own merits before merge.
summary: APPROVED. AWS: all 7 cache-bypassing AwsClientProvider methods now route through clientCache.computeIfAbsent with correct HOST:/HOST_TOKEN:/ROLE: keys; getHostDynamoDbClient uses a single cached client with an auto-refreshing StsAssumeRoleCredentialsProvider and no longer calls stsClient.assumeRole per invocation; withPermissionTracking/getClientOverrideConfig/getFinOpsClientOverrideConfig/evictAccount are untouched; regions/credentials/overrides preserved. Azure: no per-call HttpClient.newHttpClient() remains on request paths in AzureDbOpsService/AzurePerformanceService/AzureAlertsService/AzureSecurityService/AzureReservationService — all route through the shared, pooled, timeout-configured AzureArmClient, with URIs, api-versions, nextLink pagination, bearer auth, and 403->PERMISSION_ERROR / other->API_ERROR / 404->null / empty->NO_DATA mappings preserved; buildRecommendations keeps its own paged loop on one constructor-built reused client (documented minimum fallback) because armClient.get cannot distinguish its 400/204 branches. GCP: caching was deliberately reverted (documented in FEAT-003) because ~97 call sites already close provider clients via try-with-resources; verified no gapic *.create() exists outside GcpClientProvider, so GCP is already leak-safe and nothing caches/closes a shared client. Build and tests are green: 'mvn -q -pl xamops-service -am compile' succeeds and 'mvn -pl xamops-service -am test' => Tests run: 3385, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 (incl. the new AwsClientProviderCachingTest, 6 tests). One latent non-blocking issue noted in getEksClientForTokenGeneration (dead code) plus three unrelated security/cost commits bundled in the branch.
